item.title: Barn owls, bees, puffins and hedgehogs to feature on UK banknotes
item.description: Barn owls, bumblebees, puffins and hedgehogs will feature on new Bank of England banknotes over the coming years, replacing World War Two leader Winston Churchill and other historic figures, the Bank of England said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: David Milliken
item.content:encoded: Barn owls, bumblebees, puffins and hedgehogs will feature on new Bank of England banknotes over the coming years, replacing World War Two leader Winston Churchill and other historic figures, the Bank of England said on Thursday. The BoE's decision in March to [USN:L8N3ZY174 TEXT:"no longer feature famous Britons"] on future banknotes, in favour of native wildlife, dismayed politicians across the political spectrum and prompted speculation that the central bank wanted to avoid controversies around historic figures. The BoE said the change would make its banknotes more distinctive and harder to counterfeit, and followed a public consultation where people had been invited to choose between different categories of images. Almost 500,000 people voted on a [USN:L8N4291CL TEXT:"selection of 18 animals"] released by the central bank in June. The buff-tailed bumblebee was the most popular creature on the shortlist, followed by the barn owl and the European hedgehog. Red foxes and common kingfishers received more votes than the Atlantic puffin, which the BoE selected to ensure a marine animal was on the list. "I am delighted that nearly half a million people responded to our wildlife imagery consultation, showing that cash still matters," BoE Chief Cashier Victoria Cleland said. Cash usage has fallen steeply in Britain in recent years, accelerated by the COVID-19 pandemic which led to almost all retailers accepting contactless card and smartphone payments. Under 10% of payments were made by cash in 2024, but trade body UK Finance said it expected the decline to level off as a small percentage of Britons strongly preferred to use cash. The new banknotes will continue to feature the monarch. The £5 Churchill note, issued in 2016, is the first due to be replaced, followed by the £10 with novelist Jane Austen, £20 with artist JMW Turner and £50 with mathematician Alan Turing.

item.title: Blues, Sharks meet after enduring rough performances
item.description: The St. Louis Blues hope a return home can spark the offense when the San Jose Sharks visit on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The St. Louis Blues hope a return home can spark the offense when the San Jose Sharks visit on Thursday. The Blues' season began with a three-game road trip, and the initial success of a 4-0 shutout over the Dallas Stars. St. Louis then lost its next two games while being outscored 10-3, including Tuesday's 4-2 loss to the Chicago Blackhawks. Despite a 13-4 shots edge in the third period and a 27-21 shots advantage in the game as a whole, the Blues couldn't mount a comeback against Chicago. St. Louis is averaging 19 even-strength shots per game, and four of the team's seven goals have come in 5-on-5 play. Connor McMichael leads St. Louis with three points (one goal, two assists). Robert Thomas and Dylan Holloway led the Blues in goals last season, but the forwards are each still looking for their first point of the new campaign. Tuesday was "a game we feel like we can step up and take over, so yeah, it is frustrating. You feel like you're letting the group down," Thomas told The Athletic. "But that's the beauty of the league. We're playing again tomorrow night and we have another opportunity to do it in our home opener." San Jose is also looking to bounce back after one of its worst-ever offensive games. The Sharks were outshot 26-13 in Monday's 5-0 loss to Dallas, tying the eighth-lowest shot total in franchise history. Since the Sharks scored nine times while winning their first two games of the season, Macklin Celebrini's absence stands out as the obvious reason for Monday's struggles. Celebrini took part in the warm-up skate on Monday but was a late scratch from the lineup due to a lower-body injury. Celebrini didn't practice on Tuesday or Wednesday, and Sharks coach Ryan Warsofsky told San Jose Hockey Now on Tuesday that the forward is day-to-day. Warsofsky described the unspecified injury as "something we've been trying to manage here a little bit." It remains uncertain if Celebrini will face the Blues, but "our identity doesn't change whether Mack's in the lineup or not. He's a great player, we know that, but we need guys to step up and fill some spots," Warsofsky said. Celebrini has five assists in two games, leading the Sharks in both helpers and points. Will Smith and Igor Chernyshov share the team's goal lead with two apiece. Yaroslav Askarov has been in net for all three of San Jose's games, posting an .862 save percentage and 3.86 goals-against average. After allowing five goals on 26 Dallas shots, Askarov may get a rest Thursday so backup goalie Alex Nedeljkovic could get his first action of the season. Joel Hofer has started two of the Blues' three games, with Jordan Binnington starting last Saturday's 6-1 loss to the Colorado Avalanche. Binnington would be lined up to face the Sharks if St. Louis is using a strict goalie rotation, though Hofer finished last season as the team's preferred choice in net. Veteran defenseman Colton Parayko is expected to play Thursday in his 804th game with the Blues, the second-most in franchise history. He's currently tied with Barret Jackman. The Sharks have a nine-game points streak (5-0-4) against the Blues over the previous three seasons. --Field Level Media

item.title: Blackhawks playing inspired hockey, next take on Islanders
item.description: The Chicago Blackhawks got a glimpse Tuesday night of what they envisioned when they brought back three-time Stanley Cup champion Patrick Kane to mentor their young roster.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Chicago Blackhawks got a glimpse Tuesday night of what they envisioned when they brought back three-time Stanley Cup champion Patrick Kane to mentor their young roster. For the New York Islanders and defenseman Alexander Romanov, Tuesday night represented the worst-case scenario for a second straight season. The Blackhawks look to win their second straight game, while the Islanders begin adjusting to life without Romanov, when Chicago visits the New York Islanders on Thursday night in Elmont, N.Y. Both teams were off Wednesday after playing Tuesday, when the Blackhawks earned their first win by beating the visiting St. Louis Blues 4-2 and the Islanders fell to the host New York Rangers 5-2. Sam Rinzel and Anton Frondell gave the Blackhawks the lead for good by scoring within a two-minute span early in the second for Chicago, which was outscored 15-5 by the Vegas Golden Knights, Utah Mammoth and Buffalo Sabres during a season-opening road trip. "A lot of times, to get that first win when you haven't won in a few, you've got to kind of grind it out," Blackhawks head coach Jeff Blashill said. "You probably feel a little bit of that weight (lifted). Now we've got to build on it." Chicago's roster features six first-round draft picks selected since 2022, including Rinzel (2022, 25th overall) and Frondell (2025, third). Frank Nazar, who was also a first-round pick in 2022 (13th), provided insurance against St. Louis by scoring an empty-netter in the final five seconds. Artyom Levshunov, a 2024 first-round selection (second overall), had the primary assist on Frondell's go-ahead goal. In addition, center Connor Bedard, picked first overall in the 2023 draft, is recovering from left shoulder surgery in July. Chicago has missed the playoffs in eight of the last nine seasons and hasn't advanced past the first round since 2015, when Kane helped the Blackhawks win the Stanley Cup for the third time in six seasons. The Blackhawks selected Kane first overall in the 2007 draft before trading him to the New York Rangers in 2023. Kane spent the previous three seasons with the Detroit Red Wings before signing a two-year deal with Chicago as a free agent in July. The 37-year-old right winger received a lengthy standing ovation during a video tribute prior to faceoff Tuesday, when he had two shots in just under 21 minutes on ice. The Blackhawks will be without Teuvo Teravainen, who sustained a lower-body injury Tuesday. Blashill said the forward would not accompany the team to New York. The Islanders, who missed the playoffs for the second straight year last spring, showed a hint of their potential in their home opener Saturday, when New York routed the New Jersey Devils 6-0. But the Islanders never led Tuesday, falling behind the Rangers 2-0 before Bo Horvat and Cal Ritchie scored within 1:56 early in the second. They had just eight shots the rest of the way, including five in the third, when Alexis Lafreniere iced the win for the Rangers by collecting two empty-net goals in the final 1:38. "We had a chance to take the lead -- that maybe changes the game," Islanders head coach Peter DeBoer said. "It's not easy in this league playing from behind." The third period will likely be the final regular-season action for Romanov, who exited with 12:04 left. The Islanders announced Wednesday that Romanov tore the ACL in his right knee and will require surgery that will sideline him for six to eight months. It will be a second straight lost season for Romanov, who missed the final 62 games last year due to a left shoulder injury sustained against the Dallas Stars on Nov. 18. --Field Level Media

item.title: Samsung Q3 profit jumps nearly nine-fold as AI memory boom lifts chip earnings
item.description: Samsung Electronics on Thursday projected a nearly nine-fold jump in third-quarter operating profit from a year earlier, beating analysts' estimates as booming demand for artificial intelligence chips drove strong memory earnings.
item.dc:creator: Heekyong Yang, Joyce Lee
item.content:encoded: Samsung Electronics (005930.KS) on Thursday projected a nearly nine-fold jump in third-quarter operating profit from a year earlier, beating analysts' estimates as booming demand for artificial intelligence chips drove strong memory earnings. The world's largest memory chipmaker estimated an operating profit of 107.4 trillion won ($80.17 billion) for the July-September period, compared with an LSEG SmartEstimate of 106.1 trillion won, a regulatory filing showed. Samsung's fourth consecutive quarter of [USN:L4N45O0LB TEXT:"record operating profit"], up from 12.17 trillion won a year earlier, underscores how soaring demand for AI infrastructure has outstripped memory chip supply growth, a gap expected to persist into 2027. Prices have soared due to the tight supply of conventional DRAM and NAND chips as well as growing demand for high-bandwidth memory (HBM), essential for processing vast amounts of data for AI applications. Third-quarter revenue would likely rise 127% to 195 trillion won from a year earlier, Samsung said. The company will release detailed results, including a breakdown of earnings by business division, on October 29. Memory chips are expected to account for the bulk of the earnings improvement. Analysts expect supply to continue to lag demand, with the imbalance potentially widening in 2027 as AI-related demand absorbs an increasing share of global memory capacity. Against that backdrop, conventional DRAM bit shipments are expected to remain broadly flat because of limited inventories, while HBM shipments could rise sharply from the previous quarter on strong demand for HBM4, analysts said. Douglas Kim of Douglas Research Advisory estimated that Samsung's HBM bit shipments expanded by close to 50% quarter-over-quarter in the third quarter. However, a stronger South Korean won may have offset some of those gains by reducing the value of dollar-denominated overseas sales when converted into local currency. The memory chip boom also presents a challenge for Samsung's other businesses, particularly its smartphone and consumer electronics divisions, which face mounting pressure from higher component costs. Higher memory prices, while benefiting Samsung's semiconductor arm, are raising costs for its own smartphones and other electronic devices, squeezing margins in those businesses. ($1 = 1,339.5700 won)

item.title: STF exclui créditos presumidos de ICMS da base de cálculo do PIS e da Cofins
item.description: O Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) decidiu nesta quarta-feira que créditos fiscais presumidos de ICMS não podem ser incluídos na base de cálculo do Programa de Integração Social (PIS) e da Contribuição para Financiamento da Seguridade Social (Cofins), segundo comunicado da corte.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) decidiu nesta quarta-feira que créditos fiscais presumidos de ICMS não podem ser incluídos na base de cálculo do Programa de Integração Social (PIS) e da Contribuição para Financiamento da Seguridade Social (Cofins), segundo comunicado da corte. A decisão, aguardada há muito por empresas do país e que pode implicar em impacto bilionário nas contas do governo federal, foi tomada no julgamento do Recurso Extraordinário (RE) 835818, com repercussão geral reconhecida. O crédito é um benefício fiscal dado por Estados para incentivar cadeias econômicas e o setor privado defendia que ele não poderia ser incluído na base para se calcular o ICMS devido uma vez que ele é resultado de desconto de tributação decidida por governos estaduais. Segundo a maioria do Plenário do STF, os créditos "não representam riqueza própria da empresa e, portanto, não podem ser considerados faturamento, nem receita para fins de incidência do PIS e da Cofins". O STF afirmou no comunicado que na sessão desta quarta-feira o ministro Dias Toffoli alterou seu entendimento para acompanhar essa posição, citando que tal avaliação poderia gerar insegurança jurídica. Atualmente há milhares de processos no Brasil sobre o assunto. Ao elaborar o projeto de orçamento deste ano, o governo federal estimou em R$16,5 bilhões o impacto de uma derrota no caso. A Procuradoria-Geral da Fazenda Nacional (PGFN) afirmou que vai esperar a publicação do acórdão do julgamento para avaliar eventuais recursos contra a decisão, mas citou que o resultado vai contra decisões anteriores do próprio STF. "O resultado do julgamento foi formado com a participação de quatro votos proferidos por ministros que já não integram o tribunal, dentre eles o voto original do relator (Marco Aurélio)", afirmou a PGFN se referindo também aos ministros aposentados Rosa Weber, Ricardo Lewandowski e Luís Roberto Barroso. "Esse cenário fez com que a composição atual do STF não participasse integralmente do debate e da construção do entendimento final", acrescentou a procuradoria citando "preocupação institucional".

item.title: Saints QB Tyler Shough dealing with sore left hand, expects to play Sunday
item.description: New Orleans quarterback Tyler Shough doesn't expect his sore left hand to prevent him from playing on Sunday against the Minnesota Vikings.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: New Orleans quarterback Tyler Shough doesn't expect his sore left hand to prevent him from playing on Sunday against the Minnesota Vikings. Shough's non-throwing hand was wrapped during the team's walk-through on Wednesday, when he was listed as limited in an estimation of availability. He hurt the hand when it was hit during the Saints' 45-24 home loss to the Atlanta Falcons on Monday night. "Yeah, just something to keep working on," Shough, 27, said on a video from the team. "Just got it banged up in the game. Nothing different than anybody else is dealing with quite honestly. Just bumps and bruises and stuff like that." He played the entire game, completing 30 of 48 passes (62.5%) for 286 yards and one touchdown. The Falcons recorded 12 quarterback hits and two sacks. "It's a shorter week, so I'm obviously sore today, but it's not going to limit me really at all," Shough said of the 1-3 Saints' home game against the Vikings (4-0). Shough has played all 306 offensive snaps for New Orleans this season and leads the league with 121 completions and 180 attempts. He has thrown for 1,203 yards, nine touchdowns and three interceptions. Shough also has rushed 16 times for 72 yards and one TD. He made the NFL All-Rookie Team in 2025, completing 67.6% of his passes for 2,384 yards, 10 TDs and six picks in 11 games. He went 5-4 as a starter. New Orleans running back Alvin Kamara (back), wide receiver Chris Olave (rest), linebacker Kaden Elliss (calf), edge rusher Anfernee Jennings (knee) and wide receiver/return specialist Barion Brown (thigh) were listed as did not practice on Wednesday's injury report. --Field Level Media

item.title: Padres closer Mason Miller returns from paternity list for Game 4
item.description: The San Diego Padres activated All-Star closer Mason Miller from the paternity list prior to Wednesday night's Game 4 of the National League Division Series against the visiting Milwaukee Brewers.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The San Diego Padres activated All-Star closer Mason Miller from the paternity list prior to Wednesday night's Game 4 of the National League Division Series against the visiting Milwaukee Brewers. Miller was placed on the list Tuesday, hours before the Padres recorded a 4-3 victory to remain alive in the best-of-five series. Starting pitcher Michael King filled Miller's closing role with two shutout innings. "Everything went well so far with him and his wife and he should be back," Padres manager Craig Stammen told reporters shortly before the Padres officially announced Miller's return. The right-handed Miller blew the save in Game 2 on Sunday when the Padres fell 4-3 in Milwaukee. He was asked to get six outs for the first time all season and he was able to get only five before serving up Jackson Chourio's game-winning, two-run single. Left-handed setup man Adrian Morejon (shoulder) is expected back Wednesday after being unavailable in Game 3. The Padres removed left-hander Wandy Peralta from the roster for Miller's return. Miller is 0-1 with one save and a 6.75 ERA in two appearances this postseason. San Diego right-hander Walker Buehler (9-6, 4.83 ERA in the regular season) and left-hander Robert Gasser (5-5, 3.87) are the Game 4 starters. Gasser was in the Padres' system before being traded to the Brewers in August 2022 as part of the package in which left-handed reliever Josh Hader went to San Diego. Gasser has never faced his former team. Milwaukee leads the series 2-1 and can wrap it up with a victory Wednesday in San Diego. --Field Level Media

item.title: Hegseth praises sailors' resilience after record-breaking carrier deployment
item.description: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth flew to the flight deck of the aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln on Wednesday and praised the resilience of sailors who endured an extended, wartime deployment that drew scrutiny over suicide attempts on board.
item.dc:creator: Phil Stewart
item.content:encoded: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth flew to the flight deck of the aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln on Wednesday and praised the resilience of sailors who endured an extended, wartime deployment that drew scrutiny over suicide attempts on board. The Lincoln, which is due to dock on Thursday in San Diego, is the flagship of a carrier strike group that had [USN:L1N45G0IP TEXT:"eight suicide attempts"] among US sailors during its time at sea, according to the Navy. Its deployment included more than 260 continuous days without a port call, a record, according to the Pentagon. Hegseth, whose speeches regularly target the media, accused reporters of trying to turn the crew of the Lincoln strike group into symbols of dysfunction or of a failed mission instead of heroes of the conflict, and presented a citation from President Donald Trump for their achievements during the Iran war. The Lincoln's accomplishments included sinking 64 Iranian warships, destroying 21 anti-ship cruise missiles, executing 3,693 combat sorties, launching 450 Tomahawk land attack cruise missiles and firing 1.37 million pounds of ordnance against Iran, Hegseth said. Despite the fast pace of combat operations, it suffered no casualties and had no aircraft mishaps, Hegseth said. "What makes the US military and the US Navy and all these sailors different is that you adapt and that you're resilient and you overcome - you finish the mission nonetheless," Hegseth told the crew. "Yes, it's hard. That's why you're here. You do difficult and hard things." Typically naval deployments are for between six and nine months but can be extended during times of conflict. Mental health issues on long deployments have long challenged the US Navy. In August, amid reports of low morale and supply shortages on board, Trump was asked whether he thought the Lincoln had been deployed too long. Trump responded: "No, no, no. Not nearly long enough." Hegseth acknowledged some challenges on board, saying "there wasn't an easy resupply." Ahead of the carrier's return to port, Hegseth joked that he was "the only thing standing between you and home" and that he was also the one who signed the orders repeatedly extending the deployment. "You deserve to see your families and see them as soon as possible," Hegseth said, adding he just wanted to see them for "a moment on the route, on the way in, just to say thank you." The carrier's return comes at a crossroads in the US-Iran war, which has jolted global energy markets and become a political liability for Trump and fellow Republicans ahead of November midterm elections . The war — and its [USN:L6N4530XO TEXT:"$3 billion monthly price tag"] — has become a key issue on the campaign trail. Higher energy prices have put Trump and Republicans on the defensive in competitive states that will decide control of Congress. Trump is weighing next steps against Iran, including whether to escalate strikes before or after the elections, as he presses a naval blockade meant to pile economic pressure on Tehran to reach a deal to end the conflict. Vice President JD Vance [USN:L6N45S099 TEXT:"told Reuters"] on Monday that Iran must make a "meaningful" reduction in its uranium enrichment capacity to satisfy US demands and end the countries' seven-month war. Hegseth said the crew of the Lincoln had helped ensure the US objective of preventing Iran from acquiring a nuclear weapon. "You have changed the arc of history," he told them on Wednesday.

item.title: Trump floats turning his Florida golf course into presidential retreat
item.description: US President Donald Trumpon Wednesday backed a plan to turn part of his West Palm Beach, Florida, golf course into a Camp David-style presidential retreat.
item.dc:creator: Christian Martinez, Bo Erickson
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump on Wednesday backed a plan to turn part of his West Palm Beach, Florida, golf course into a Camp David-style presidential retreat. "It's a great idea, and it will be used a lot," Trump told reporters on Wednesday when asked about the plan. "The advantage is — this was suggested to me by the military and Secret Service — there are no high buildings looming over it," Trump told reporters. He also noted the location's proximity to the recently renamed President Donald J. Trump International Airport and a lack of nearby housing. "They asked if I'd be willing to do it, and I said I would be," Trump said. "This wouldn't be for me. This would be for all future presidents." The club was the site of a foiled assassination attempt on Trump in 2024. Ryan Routh was [USN:L6N3YZ0D3 TEXT:"sentenced to life in prison"] in February after prosecutors said he hid in bushes near the course with a semi-automatic rifle. Secret Service agents captured him before he could fire a shot. The Palm Beach Post first reported that a lawyer representing Trump International Golf Club proposed the idea in a letter last month to Palm Beach County officials. The plan would designate a parcel of the club as a permanent location for presidents and world leaders, the newspaper said. Reuters could not immediately confirm the letter's contents. An attorney representing the club told the Washington Post that Trump would pay for construction of the presidential residence and facilities. The US Secret Service and Department of Defense did not immediately respond to a request for comment. (This story has refiled to remove the extraneous word 'secret' in paragraph 5.)

item.title: Prefeito francês flagrado em vídeo viral de confronto diz que estudantes manifestantes “podiam ser meus filhos”
item.description: Em um vídeo que se tornou viral nas redes sociais, Bally Bagayoko, prefeito da cidade francesa de Saint-Denis, aparece de frente para a polícia durante uma marcha em Paris na terça-feira, protegendo jovens manifestantes e gritando “parem”.
item.dc:creator: Layli Foroudi
item.content:encoded: Em um vídeo que se tornou viral nas redes sociais, Bally Bagayoko, prefeito da cidade francesa de Saint-Denis, aparece de frente para a polícia durante uma marcha em Paris na terça-feira, protegendo jovens manifestantes e gritando “parem”. Bagayoko disse que vem apoiando os estudantes em seu subúrbio parisiense de classe trabalhadora e que, na terça-feira, pediu à polícia que não avançasse. “Eles decidiram avançar e, de fato, perseguir os estudantes, muitos dos quais não haviam demonstrado qualquer comportamento agressivo em relação aos policiais”, disse Bagayoko, que faz parte do partido de extrema-esquerda França Insubmissa (LFI), à Reuters em uma entrevista nesta quarta-feira em seu gabinete na prefeitura de Saint-Denis, na periferia norte de Paris. No fim, a polícia lançou gás lacrimogêneo contra o grupo, incluindo o prefeito, disse ele. A onda de protestos estudantis, que começou nos subúrbios marginalizados de Paris, já dura mais de duas semanas e revelou uma indignação pública generalizada a seis meses das eleições para substituir o presidente francês, Emmanuel Macron. Houve mais de 6.000 prisões e dezenas de estudantes feridos desde o início dos protestos. Grupos de direitos humanos e sindicatos acusam a polícia de usar táticas repressivas contra menores, incluindo o uso de cassetetes, gás lacrimogêneo e armas não letais do tipo “flashball”. As autoridades afirmam que centenas de policiais também ficaram feridos, escolas foram incendiadas ou saqueadas, e professores e cidadãos foram atacados. A cidade de Saint-Denis, onde os índices de pobreza são mais do que o dobro da média nacional, foi um dos primeiros locais dos protestos estudantis no final de setembro contra salas de aula superlotadas e insalubres, falta de professores e desigualdade de oportunidades. “Os protestos não são novidade por aqui, acontecem sempre no início do ano letivo”, disse Bagayoko. “A promessa republicana (de igualdade) — especialmente para os bairros da classe trabalhadora e também para as áreas rurais — não está sendo respeitada.” Ele afirmou que o governo deveria priorizar o investimento em educação e cobrar impostos mais pesados dos bilionários. O primeiro-ministro francês, Sébastien Lecornu, disse nesta quarta-feira que o governo analisaria as reivindicações dos estudantes e apresentaria propostas no final de outubro, mas não deu detalhes. O governo sugeriu que políticos do LFI estariam por trás dos protestos, uma acusação que Bagayoko rejeitou como insultuosa aos jovens manifestantes. Pai de quatro filhos, ele disse que “os alunos do ensino médio que estavam nas ruas poderiam ser meus filhos... é minha responsabilidade estar ao lado deles”.

item.title: FBI arrests man for plotting mass shooting at Mall of America
item.description: The FBI has arrested an 18-year-old man who had been plotting to carry out a mass shooting at the Mall of America near Minneapolis in the name of ISIS, according to court filings.
item.dc:creator: Dan Rosenzweig-Ziff
item.content:encoded: The FBI has arrested an 18-year-old man who had been plotting to carry out a mass shooting at the Mall of America near Minneapolis in the name of ISIS, according to court filings. He was arrested on Tuesday after an FBI undercover agent sold the Minnesota man, Sheikhdoon Abdullahi Mohamud, an AK-47, ammunition and magazines for $600, according to the complaint. Mohamud told the informant he planned to use the items to kill 30 to 60 people at an event at the mall in late October. Mohamud was charged with one count of knowingly receiving a firearm and ammunition in order to commit an act of terrorism. His lawyer did not immediately respond to a request for comment. According to the complaint, Mohamud told an FBI source on various messaging platforms that he intended to travel overseas to fight on behalf of al-Shabaab, a designated foreign terrorist organization. He said if he couldn't travel, he planned to conduct a mass shooting. He later said he wanted to join ISIS. He also allegedly expressed support for a man who rammed a truck into a crowd in New Orleans on January 1, 2025, killing 14, before being killed in a shootout with police. In July, Mohamud allegedly said he wanted to kill 30 to 60 people at the Mall of America because he claimed its owners were Jewish, and he wanted to kill non-Muslims. He told the informant he planned an attack for October 24 because there was a "Hmong Arts Celebration" that day at the mall. The Mall of America is the largest mall in the United States, with a theme park, an aquarium and more than 500 stores. On Tuesday, Mohamud allegedly bought the AK-47, four 30-round-capacity magazines and about 200 rounds of ammunition from an FBI undercover agent. Soon after, FBI agents arrested him. Mohamud made his initial court appearance before US Magistrate Judge Elizabeth Cowan Wright on Wednesday.

item.title: TikTok gave teens, children placebo safety feature in experiment, New York alleges
item.description: TikTok ran an experiment on thousands of users who tried to turn on a safety feature on the platform, giving them non-functional versions of the tool, according to allegations in New York’s lawsuit against the company unsealed on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Diana Jones
item.content:encoded: TikTok ran an experiment on thousands of users who tried to turn on a safety feature on the platform, giving them non-functional versions of the tool, according to allegations in New York’s lawsuit against the company unsealed on Wednesday. In the so-called “ghost” or placebo experiments, TikTok selected thousands of users, including teens and children, who opted to use safety features like “Algo Refresh,” a tool designed to reset recommendations for users seeking to escape unwanted or potentially harmful content. According to the lawsuit, those users believed they had activated the feature, but their feeds did not change, unlike users who got the fully working version. The newly unsealed allegations are part of New York Attorney General Letitia James’ lawsuit against the company, one of more than two dozen brought by states accusing TikTok of designing its platform to addict children and of misleading users about its safety. Many documents in state cases across the country have been sealed or heavily redacted as TikTok has sought to keep details about its operations from public view. The lawsuit claims TikTok assures users that safety is a top priority and that its platform is appropriate for kids and teens, while knowingly preventing some groups of users from accessing certain safety tools, including users who had specifically sought to avoid unwanted or potentially harmful content. "We continuously make improvements to our platform which means that, like most companies, we regularly test new products and features to validate the experience and understand how they work in the real world," a TikTok spokesperson said in a statement. The company has broadly denied New York's allegations in court filings and has said that keeping young users safe is a priority. In September, TikTok [USN:FWN45H0LS TEXT:"settled the first state lawsuit"] set for trial, agreeing to pay Alabama up to $300 million and change how its platform functions for teens in the state. James, a Democrat, originally sued in 2024. The claims about the tests were included in an updated, sealed version of New York’s complaint filed at the end of August and later ordered unsealed by a judge. EMPLOYEE FLAGGED TEST Internally, a product manager for Digital Well Being at TikTok, said doing placebo tests on the Algo Refresh feature was problematic and that users might find it misleading, the lawsuit alleges. “This feature is about algorithm transparency and control,” the person wrote in an internal chat, according to the lawsuit. “A placebo group completely conflicts with that.” Ultimately the company did the tests repeatedly on thousands of users in 2023, comparing users who did not get the feature with those who did, to study how long users stayed on the site and the impact on ad revenue, the lawsuit alleges. The lawsuit also alleges that TikTok misled consumers about how “Algo Refresh” worked, telling them it would reset the algorithm that recommended videos to them when it was only a temporary change. The TikTok spokesperson said the allegations mischaracterize how "Algo Refresh" works. The unsealed portions of the lawsuit also allege that TikTok conducted a separate set of experiments, which were previously revealed in a report by Bloomberg. In them, TikTok randomly selected users and turned off safety features on their accounts that limited their exposure to harmful content. A teen boy in New York who was part of the test committed suicide after he was shown content about self-harm and suicide, Bloomberg reported. Internal reviews showed the boy had been shown an “onslaught” of content about suicide and self-harm, the lawsuit said.

item.title: Milho e soja recuam em Chicago com avanço da colheita nos EUA
item.description: Os contratos futuros de milho e soja de Chicago recuaram em relação às máximas de uma semana nesta quarta-feira, pressionados pelo avanço da colheita no Meio-Oeste dos EUA, pelo dólar forte e pela incerteza antes dos relatórios mensais de oferta e demanda agrícola que serão divulgados pelo Departamento de Agricultura dos EUA nesta sexta-feira, segundo analistas.
item.dc:creator: Julie Ingwersen
item.content:encoded: Os contratos futuros de milho e soja de Chicago recuaram em relação às máximas de uma semana nesta quarta-feira, pressionados pelo avanço da colheita no Meio-Oeste dos EUA, pelo dólar forte e pela incerteza antes dos relatórios mensais de oferta e demanda agrícola que serão divulgados pelo Departamento de Agricultura dos EUA nesta sexta-feira, segundo analistas. Os futuros do trigo recuaram mais de 2% devido a vendas técnicas e à incerteza sobre a demanda, à medida que a moeda norte-americana se fortaleceu. O contrato de milho para dezembro fechou em queda de 6 centavos, ou 1,2%, a US$5,02 o bushel, e o contrato de soja para novembro encerrou com queda de 5,50 centavos, ou 0,4%, a US$12,975 o bushel. O contrato de trigo de dezembro fechou em queda de 17,75 centavos, ou 2,5%, a US$6,865 por bushel. O milho e a soja recuaram à medida que as colheitadeiras avançavam pelo Meio-Oeste sob um céu predominantemente claro, ampliando os trabalhos no campo após as fortes chuvas do final de setembro terem atrasado o andamento das atividades. Os mercados à vista do Meio-Oeste para ambas as culturas permaneceram fracos nesta semana, com o aumento das vendas por parte dos agricultores. "Estamos entrando em uma fase de colheita intensa aqui", disse Don Roose, presidente da U.S. Commodities, com sede em Iowa, acrescentando que os participantes do mercado estavam acompanhando os relatórios de rendimento dos campos antes dos relatórios de oferta e demanda do USDA, que incluirão estimativas atualizadas para os EUA. Analistas consultados pela Reuters esperam, em média, que o USDA reduza na sexta-feira sua estimativa do rendimento médio do milho nos EUA, mantendo inalterada a previsão para a produtividade da soja.

item.title: Maduro enfrentará novas acusações dos EUA por suposta tortura de norte-americanos, diz autoridade
item.description: O ex-presidente venezuelano Nicolás Maduro e sua esposa, Cilia Flores, devem enfrentar novas acusações criminais nos EUA por supostas torturas contra cidadãos norte-americanos detidos naquele país sul-americano, afirmou uma autoridade norte-americana nesta quarta-feira.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Goudsward, Luc Cohen
item.content:encoded: O ex-presidente venezuelano Nicolás Maduro e sua esposa, Cilia Flores, devem enfrentar novas acusações criminais nos EUA por supostas torturas contra cidadãos norte-americanos detidos naquele país sul-americano, afirmou uma autoridade norte-americana nesta quarta-feira. As novas acusações podem ser apresentadas já na quinta-feira, segundo a autoridade, que foi informada sobre a investigação. Maduro e Flores foram capturados por forças dos EUA em suas residências em Caracas no dia 3 de janeiro e levados para Nova York para responder a acusações de tráfico de drogas. Eles se declararam inocentes. Um porta-voz da procuradoria federal de Manhattan, que apresentou as acusações, se recusou a comentar. Os advogados de Maduro e Flores não responderam imediatamente aos pedidos de comentário. A possibilidade de novas acusações foi divulgada pela primeira vez pela CNN nesta quarta-feira. Detalhes das novas acusações, incluindo as identidades das supostas vítimas de tortura, não foram divulgados imediatamente. Os 13 anos de Maduro no poder na Venezuela, país rico em petróleo, foram marcados por tensões com os Estados Unidos. Washington afirmou que vários de seus cidadãos foram detidos injustamente no país sul-americano durante seu mandato. Desde a captura de Maduro, a Venezuela tem sido liderada por sua ex-vice-presidente, Delcy Rodríguez, que intensificou a cooperação com o governo Trump.

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: General Dynamics (GD.N) on Wednesday said President Danny Deep would take over as CEO in January, succeeding longtime chief executive Phebe Novakovic. The leadership transition comes at a time of sustained demand for the company's defense and aerospace products, which range from Gulfstream jets and submarines to combat vehicles and IT services. Here are more details: Deep held senior leadership roles across General Dynamics' land systems, combat systems and global operations businesses before being named president in 2025 Novakovic, who will become executive chairman, has been General Dynamics' CEO since 2013, steering the company through a decade of growth and rising global defense spending The defense contractor [USN:L4N43V11A TEXT:"reported"] profit of $4.24 per share for the quarter ended July 5, above analysts' estimate of $3.97, according to data compiled by LSEG

item.title: Commanders QB Jayden Daniels to 'embrace the brace,' play vs. Giants
item.description: Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels was a full participant in practice Wednesday, another step toward his return from a left elbow injury.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels was a full participant in practice Wednesday, another step toward his return from a left elbow injury. Daniels hurt his non-throwing arm on the final play of the first half in Week 2 against the Dallas Cowboys and traveled with the Commanders (1-3) to London last week. He was limited in every practice before the loss to the Indianapolis Colts, when starter Marcus Mariota went down with a sprained knee. Rookie Athan Kaliakmanis replaced Mariota, but Daniels took the reps in Wednesday's practice. Head coach Dan Quinn confirmed he plans to start Daniels this week against the visiting New York Giants (3-1), barring any setbacks. "The goal is for him to have a full week of practice and start on Sunday," Quinn said. "We won't put him out there before he's ready." Part of getting ready was beginning work in Wednesday's practice on protecting his elbow. Quinn said there are some adjustments for Daniels to make and others for the team to address. Daniels wore a brace on his left elbow and plans to keep it on for game day. "I'm gonna embrace the brace," Daniels said. "Go out there and be the best version of myself." Daniels, 25, missed time last season with the same injury and was forced to exit his first game back in 2025 after spraining the same elbow. He played a total of only seven games last season due to multiple injuries. He has completed only 57% of his passes this season (29 of 51) but has three touchdowns and no turnovers in six quarters of game action in 2026. He is 3-0 in his career against the Giants. "Just putting in the countless hours of work and preparation," Daniels said. "Just go out there and give myself the best opportunity to perform to the best of my ability on Sunday." The Commanders hosted former United Football League MVP quarterback Jack Plummer on Wednesday morning, according to the league transactions log. --Field Level Media

item.title: Trump diz que merece Prêmio Nobel da Paz, mas tem dúvidas sobre suas chances
item.description: O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, que trava uma guerra contra o Irã e ainda não conseguiu negociar a paz na Ucrânia, afirmou nesta quarta-feira que deveria ganhar o Prêmio Nobel da Paz, mas reconheceu ter dúvidas quanto às suas chances.
item.dc:creator: Doina Chiacu, Bo Erickson
item.content:encoded: O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, que trava uma guerra contra o Irã e ainda não conseguiu negociar a paz na Ucrânia, afirmou nesta quarta-feira que deveria ganhar o Prêmio Nobel da Paz, mas reconheceu ter dúvidas quanto às suas chances. “Não sei qual será a decisão deles”, disse Trump sobre o prêmio de 2026, que o Comitê Norueguês do Nobel anunciará na sexta-feira. “Eles têm a reputação de talvez não concedê-lo a pessoas como eu.” Desde seu retorno à Casa Branca no ano passado, Trump tem afirmado repetidamente que merece o que talvez seja o prêmio mais prestigiado do mundo. “Já está na hora”, disse Trump aos repórteres no Salão Oval. “Mas fiquei muito honrado por recebê-lo indiretamente da última vez, por meio do ganhador, que disse que ninguém na história merece mais do que o presidente Trump.” A líder da oposição venezuelana María Corina Machado entregou sua medalha do Prêmio Nobel da Paz de 2025 a Trump em janeiro, enquanto buscava o apoio dos EUA para seus esforços na Venezuela. Trump afirmou que deveria receber o prêmio por ter se envolvido em oito conflitos desde que assumiu o cargo em janeiro passado. Os líderes do Camboja, de Israel e do Paquistão afirmaram ter indicado Trump, embora não haja como verificar isso. As partes envolvidas em alguns dos conflitos que Trump alega ter resolvido contestam o papel diplomático do presidente dos EUA, e os combates recomeçaram em algumas dessas regiões, incluindo a República Democrática do Congo e ao longo da fronteira entre o Camboja e a Tailândia. Uma solução para a guerra da Rússia na Ucrânia tem escapado a Trump, que prometeu encerrá-la no primeiro dia de seu segundo mandato na Casa Branca. Os ataques dos EUA e de Israel ao Irã levaram a um conflito latente de sete meses que abalou o abastecimento global de energia e elevou os preços da gasolina antes das eleições de meio de mandato de novembro. O papa Leão 14, o Tribunal Penal Internacional e o relator especial para os Territórios Palestinos estão entre os favoritos para vencer este ano.

item.title: Applied Digital's revenue soars, loss widens on growing AI investments
item.description: Applied Digital's first-quarter revenue more than quadrupled, while its net loss widened from a year earlier as the company stepped up investments to meet growing demand for data center services.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Applied Digital's (APLD.O) first-quarter revenue more than quadrupled, while its net loss widened from a year earlier as the company stepped up investments to meet growing demand for data center services. Shares of the Dallas, Texas-based company, which develops and operates data centers to support AI and other high-performance computing tasks, were up nearly 2% in volatile extended trading on Wednesday. Here are some details: Its first-quarter revenue surged to $341.9 million from $80.9 million a year earlier, surpassing analysts' average estimate of $133.8 million, according to data compiled by LSEG Net loss attributable to common stockholders stood at $221.0 million, or $0.76 per share, compared with $18.5 million, or $0.07 per share, a year earlier As of August 31, Applied Digital had $3.7 billion in cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash, along with $6.4 billion in debt Total costs and expenses jumped to $404.3 million in the quarter, from $90.7 million a year earlier Applied Digital said costs rose due to higher spending to prepare data centers for customers, increased stock-based compensation and higher interest expenses as it expanded its AI infrastructure "We are building for the long term, with a clear focus on developing large-scale, sustainable AI factory campuses and securing durable, high-quality, long-term contracts with proven, tier-one, investment-grade hyperscalers that are leaders in the AI industry," CEO Wes Cummins said in a statement

item.title: Aces G Jewell Loyd (leg) ruled out for Game 2 vs. Valkyries
item.description: Las Vegas Aces veteran guard Jewell Loyd has been ruled out of Wednesday night's Game 2 semifinal contest against the host Golden State Valkyries due to a left leg injury.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Las Vegas Aces veteran guard Jewell Loyd has been ruled out of Wednesday night's Game 2 semifinal contest against the host Golden State Valkyries due to a left leg injury. Loyd was injured during the third quarter of Game 1 on Sunday and she missed the rest of the contest. Loyd was scoreless in 17 minutes. The 2023 WNBA scoring champion, who averaged 24.7 points per game for the Seattle Storm, is now a role player for the Aces. The 12th-year pro, who turned 33 on Monday, is averaging a career-low 8.0 points per game. Loyd, a six-time All-Star, has a career average of 15.4 points per game. Las Vegas managed a season-low point total in Sunday's 71-60 loss to Golden State in Game 1 in San Francisco. Aces coach Becky Hammon mentioned being shorthanded after the loss. "We don't have a lot of time to sulk about it," Hammon said. "Nobody feels bad for us. It's the next woman up." Forward Stephanie Talbot (left leg) is questionable for Las Vegas, while guard Dana Evans (right knee) has been upgraded to probable. Both players missed Game 1. --Field Level Media

item.title: Texans coach DeMeco Ryans assumes defensive play-calling duties
item.description: The Houston Texans rode the NFL's top-ranked defense to a wild-card berth in 2025.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Houston Texans rode the NFL's top-ranked defense to a wild-card berth in 2025. They returned 10 starters from a unit that allowed a league-low 17.4 points per game. But after an 0-4 start to the 2026 season, head coach DeMeco Ryans announced Wednesday that he would take over the defensive play-calling responsibilities from coordinator Matt Burke. "If there's a lack in communication, I look at myself first, so it starts with me and making sure I'm a better communicator," Ryans said during his Wednesday news conference. "If our guys are saying communication is not right, then ultimately it falls on me. So, it's on me to get it fixed. "It's no slight against coach Burke. He's done an outstanding job. Just want to make sure I can streamline communication in the best way possible so that isn't the theme when I stand up here the next time I see you guys and talk about communication." Ryans and Burke both came to Houston in 2023, and the defense has never allowed more than 21.9 points per game. However, the Texans are 20th in yards allowed per game (343.8) and 27th in points allowed per game (27.3). The final straw came Sunday when, after holding the Dallas Cowboys to six first-half points, Houston permitted 28 in the second half of a 34-30 loss. "It's a tough decision to make. Also, as a head coach, I have a lot of tough decisions I have to make," Ryans said. "My decisions are not always a popular opinion. I'm not in this role to please a lot of people's opinions. "I have to do what's best for this team and make sure I'm leading in that way, and unfortunately, everybody isn't happy when you make changes, when you make decisions from my chair. Everybody isn't happy, and that's OK because I know everything that I try to do and strive to do is for the men in that locker room: to give those guys the best chance possible to go out and win our first football game." --Field Level Media

item.title: Preços do petróleo recuam com acordo para liberação acelerada de estoques
item.description: Os preços do petróleo fecharam em baixa nesta quarta-feira, após um pregão volátil, depois que a Agência Internacional de Energia concordou em acelerar a liberação de reservas de petróleo e priorizar o diesel, em uma tentativa de conter os preços recordes dos combustíveis, à medida que a guerra no Irã reduz a oferta global.
item.dc:creator: Georgina Mccartney
item.content:encoded: Os preços do petróleo fecharam em baixa nesta quarta-feira, após um pregão volátil, depois que a Agência Internacional de Energia concordou em acelerar a liberação de reservas de petróleo e priorizar o diesel, em uma tentativa de conter os preços recordes dos combustíveis, à medida que a guerra no Irã reduz a oferta global. Os contratos futuros do petróleo Brent fecharam com queda de 0,38%, a US$100,20 o barril. Os contratos futuros do petróleo West Texas Intermediate (WTI) dos EUA fecharam com queda de 1,3%, a US$88,28. A agência afirmou que concluir as liberações anunciadas anteriormente o mais rápido possível poderia colocar cerca de 100 milhões de barris no mercado, embora analistas e alguns governos tenham dito que o número não representava necessariamente uma nova intervenção dessa magnitude. A França liberará 10 milhões de barris de diesel de seus estoques estratégicos, informou a rádio Franceinfo nesta quarta-feira, citando fontes anônimas. Enquanto isso, os estoques de petróleo e de destilados dos EUA caíram, enquanto os estoques de gasolina aumentaram na semana passada, informou a Administração de Informações sobre Energia (EIA). Os estoques de petróleo caíram 3,2 milhões de barris, para 424,1 milhões de barris, na semana encerrada em 2 de outubro, informou o governo, em comparação com as expectativas dos analistas em uma pesquisa da Reuters que apontavam para um aumento de 1,7 milhão de barris.

item.title: Lululemon puts Nike veteran in charge of product as CEO O'Neill looks to right ship
item.description: Lululemon Athletica on Wednesday named industry veteran and former Nike vice president Maggie Gauger its chief product officer as the struggling apparel maker overhauls its leadership under new CEO Heidi O'Neill.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Lululemon Athletica (LULU.O) on Wednesday named industry veteran and former Nike vice president Maggie Gauger its chief product officer as the struggling apparel maker overhauls its leadership under new CEO Heidi O'Neill. Investors are closely watching O'Neill's turnaround plan as the sportswear maker grapples with finding its footing against newer rivals and keep pace with changing customer preferences beyond its signature leggings. Here are more details: Gauger will join Lululemon on October 26, and was most recently CEO of Gap's performance apparel brand Athleta, following a long stint at Nike, alongside O'Neill Gauger takes charge of product at Lululemon at a time the company has struggled with [USN:L4N44W0MR TEXT:"product missteps"] that have triggered consumer backlash and recalls Lululemon also appointed Joseph Godsey as chief operating officer "This is an important first step in reinvigorating our enduring connection with guests and is designed to establish the foundation for sustainable, long-term growth," O'Neill said of the appointments Lululemon's shares have nearly halved in value so far this year, and are on track for a third straight year of declines The company's net income is expected to drop nearly 40% this year from fiscal 2024, according to data compiled by LSEG Lululemon also said chief brand officer Nikki Neuburger and chief supply chain officer Ted Dagnese would leave the company, effective November 6, and that it was searching for candidates to fill the roles It added that CFO Meghan Frank would oversee global brand and technology functions until those appointments are made

item.title: Democrats sue Trump to halt taxpayer-funded TV ads that praised him
item.description: Democratic Party officials sued US President Donald Trump on Wednesday, seeking a court order blocking his administration from using taxpayer money to pay for election-related TV ads.
item.dc:creator: Jan Wolfe
item.content:encoded: Democratic Party officials sued US President Donald Trump on Wednesday, seeking a court order blocking his administration from using taxpayer money to pay for election-related TV ads. The lawsuit , filed by the Democratic National Committee in federal court in Washington, accused Trump of a "blatant violation of the statutory ban on the use of appropriations for 'publicity or propaganda purposes.'" Taxpayer-funded television ads glorifying Trump began airing in late September, sparking a bipartisan backlash. In a post on his Truth Social site on Monday, Trump [USN:FWN45R1HF TEXT:"said"] he considered the ads to be "a positive promotion for our Great U.S.A." but that they would no longer be funded by taxpayers. The White House said this week his MAGA PAC would fund the ads. The DNC, the main governing organization of the Democratic Party, said in its lawsuit that the ads continued to air after Trump's comments. "With less than 30 days remaining before the midterm election and millions of public dollars apportioned to pay for propaganda ads still unspent, the DNC has no choice but to take action in defense of free and fair elections," the lawsuit stated. The ads ran during football games as recently as Sunday and during other programming. The New York Times reported that Trump personally directed the White House budget director to use taxpayer money for the TV spots, citing sources. One ad features Trump declaring that "America will never be a communist country" while a chorus repeats the words "love me." Another combines images of Mount Rushmore with footage of Trump praising a "golden age of America." Another new ad recently has featured ousted Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro. A source briefed on the matter told Reuters the government-funded ads will end this week. The White House said Trump's political action committee will not reimburse taxpayers for the ads that have run to date. The ads end with a disclaimer saying they were paid for by the US government.

item.title: Exportação de suco de laranja do Brasil cresce quase 10% no 1º tri da safra 26/27, diz CitrusBR
item.description: As exportações brasileiras de suco de laranja pelo porto de Santos somaram 203,2 mil toneladas no primeiro trimestre da safra 2026/27, iniciada em julho, avanço anual de 9,6%, informou nesta quarta-feira a associação CitrusBR.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: As exportações brasileiras de suco de laranja pelo porto de Santos somaram 203,2 mil toneladas no primeiro trimestre da safra 2026/27, iniciada em julho, avanço anual de 9,6%, informou nesta quarta-feira a associação CitrusBR. Os dados de embarques por Santos, que concentram as exportações das associadas da CitrusBR e responderam por 92% do total embarcado pelo Brasil, indicam "alguma recuperação" nas vendas externas do maior exportador global da commodity. "Porém esse mesmo volume ainda está 14% abaixo da média das últimas cinco safras, que é de 237 mil toneladas", disse o diretor-executivo da CitrusBR, Ibiapaba Netto, em nota. O setor vem enfrentando safras ruins no Brasil nos últimos anos, embora a colheita do ano passado tenha crescido na comparação com o ano anterior, quando a produção mais baixa em décadas reduziu oferta da matéria-prima. A situação ajudou a elevar os preços do suco a níveis recordes na bolsa de referência de Nova York em 2024, afetando a demanda em mercados como a Europa. Para 2026/27, a expectativa é de nova queda na produção de laranja da principal região citrícola do Brasil, [USN:L1N452127 TEXT:"de 10%"], segundo a última projeção do fundo de pesquisas Fundecitrus. Os preços em Nova York, contudo, seguem próximos de US$1,45/libra-peso, abaixo dos mais de US$5 vistos ao final de 2024. Questionado se os resultados do primeiro trimestre da safra indicam uma recuperação consistente, em meio a preços mais baixos para os consumidores, Netto disse que ainda é cedo para tal avaliação. "Acho que a melhor parte é a recuperação parcial da Europa. Ainda está abaixo da média dos últimos cinco anos, mas é um passo...", disse ele, referindo-se ao continente europeu, antes o principal destino do suco do Brasil, lugar agora ocupado pelos Estados Unidos. Em receita, os embarques totalizaram US$489,7 milhões, uma queda de 34,4% na mesma base de comparação. Entre julho e setembro, Estados Unidos e Canadá importaram 96 mil toneladas de suco (em FCOJ equivalente a 66° Brix), ante 90,2 mil no mesmo período do ano passado. Já a Europa demandou 91,8 mil toneladas, alta de 4,8%, segundo a associação.

item.title: Medical device maker Centinel Spine discloses revenue rise in US IPO filing
item.description: Medical device maker Centinel Spine revealed a 42% rise in first-half revenue in its US initial public offering filing on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Pragyan Kalita
item.content:encoded: Medical device maker Centinel Spine revealed a 42% rise in first-half revenue in its US initial public offering filing on Wednesday. The filing comes against an uncertain backdrop for the fall IPO market, as rising bond yields and high interest rates have dampened investor appetite and prompted several major companies to delay their listings. Here are some more details: The West Chester, Pennsylvania-based company posted net income of $10.2 million on revenue of $85.2 million for the six months ended June 30, compared with a net loss of $503,000 on revenue of $60.1 million a year earlier. Centinel Spine develops replacement discs designed to preserve movement in the cervical and lumbar spine, offering an alternative to spinal fusion, which permanently eliminates motion at the treated level. Its prodisc platform has been used in more than 300,000 implantations worldwide and is supported by more than 590 peer-reviewed clinical papers, according to the company. "One of the notable factors in Centinel's filing is its ability to combine strong revenue growth with profitability, which distinguishes it from many healthcare companies approaching public markets," IPOX Research Associate Lukas Muehlbauer told Reuters. "At the same time, the company's exclusive focus on total disc replacement creates concentration risk, leaving it somewhat exposed to changes in reimbursement policies and competing technologies." Centinel Spine plans to use the offering proceeds to repay debt and invest in its sales infrastructure, patient-awareness programs, clinical trials etc. Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs, Piper Sandler, Canaccord Genuity and BTIG are underwriting the offering. It plans to list its shares on NYSE under the symbol “CNTL.”

item.title: Wolfspeed secures $1.5 billion conditional loan commitment from US defense department
item.description: Chipmaker Wolfspeed said on Wednesday it has received a conditional loan commitment for up to $1.5 billion from the US Department of Defense to expand domestic production of silicon carbide materials and power devices, sending its shares surging 27% in extended trading.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Chipmaker Wolfspeed (WOLF.N) said on Wednesday it has received a conditional loan commitment for up to $1.5 billion from the US Department of Defense to expand domestic production of silicon carbide materials and power devices, sending its shares surging 27% in extended trading. Wolfspeed makes chips using silicon carbide, which are more energy-efficient and used in applications that require huge amounts of power conversion such as electric vehicles, solar inverters and industrial power systems The company said the conditional 30-year commitment, through the defense department's Office of Strategic Capital, reflects its efforts to optimize its capital structure and improve its financial foundation It plans to use the financing to upgrade its gallium nitride technology for next-generation communications infrastructure and electronic warfare systems and develop radiation-hardening capabilities The funding is subject to due diligence, definitive agreements, government approvals and other conditions Under the proposed terms, Wolfspeed would be required to issue to the department warrants to purchase up to 7.5% of Wolfspeed's fully diluted equity

item.title: French mayor caught in viral video clash says student protesters 'could be my children'
item.description: In a video that has gone viral on social media, Bally Bagayoko, the mayor of the French town of Saint-Denis, stands facing police at a march in Paris on Tuesday, shielding young protesters and shouting "stop."
item.dc:creator: Layli Foroudi
item.content:encoded: In a video that has gone viral on social media, Bally Bagayoko, the mayor of the French town of Saint-Denis, stands facing police at a march in Paris on Tuesday, shielding young protesters and shouting "stop." Bagayoko said he has been supporting the students in his working-class Parisian suburb and on Tuesday was asking the police not to charge. "They had decided to charge and effectively go after the students, many of whom had shown no aggressive behaviour whatsoever toward the police officers," Bagayoko, who is part of the hard-left France Unbowed party (LFI), told Reuters in an interview on Wednesday at his town hall office in Saint-Denis, on the northern outskirts of Paris. In the end, the police fired tear gas at the group, including the mayor, he said. The wave of student protests, which began in [USN:L6N45M1EJ TEXT:"Paris' marginalised suburbs"], has been going on for more than two weeks and has exposed widespread public anger six months ahead of an election to replace French President Emmanuel Macron. There have been more than 6,000 arrests and dozens of student injuries since the protests began. Rights groups and unions accuse the police of using heavy-handed tactics against minors, including the use of batons, tear gas and non-lethal flashball guns. Authorities say hundreds of police officers have also been injured, schools have been burned or ransacked, and teachers and members of the public have been attacked. The town of Saint-Denis, where poverty levels are more than double the national average, was one of the first sites of student protests in late September over overcrowded and unsanitary classrooms, teacher shortages and unequal opportunities. "Protests are not new here, they happen at every start of the academic year," Bagayoko said. "The Republican promise (of equality) — in particular for the working-class neighbourhoods, and also rural areas — is not respected." He said the government should prioritise investing in education and levy heavier taxes on billionaires. Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said on Wednesday that the government would review demands made by students and present proposals at the end of October, but gave no details. The government has suggested that LFI politicians were behind the protests, an accusation that Bagayoko dismissed as insulting to the young protesters. A father of four, he said that "the high school children who were in the street could be my children ... it is my responsibility to be at their side."

item.title: Trading Day: Stocks, bonds in delicate dance
item.description: A sea of red swept across global stocks on Wednesday as the bond market selloff picked up again and lifted long-dated US yields to 24-year highs, although a strong 10-year Treasury auction and minutes of the Fed's last policy meeting eased some of the upward pressure on borrowing costs.
item.dc:creator: Jamie McGeever
item.content:encoded:
A sea of red swept across global [USN:L6N45T0JD TEXT:"stocks"] on Wednesday as the bond market selloff picked up again and lifted long-dated US yields to 24-year highs, although a strong [USN:L8N45T0F3 TEXT:"10-year Treasury auction"] and [USN:L6N45T0TQ TEXT:"minutes"] of the Fed's last policy meeting eased some of the upward pressure on borrowing costs. In [USN:L6N45S122 TEXT:"my column today"], I ask how much longer Wall Street can continue scaling fresh peaks while the bond market rout continues to push yields ever higher. It will depend on whether rising borrowing costs reflect strong growth expectations, or other risks captured by the 'term premium', which is now racing higher also. Today's Key Reads [USN:L6N45T0TQ TEXT:"Fed policymakers divided over rate-hike logic in September, minutes show "] [USN:L8N45S0RJ TEXT:"Investors pick new darlings and duds as selloff rocks Europe's bond market "] [USN:L4N45R0DE TEXT:"India joins global rate-tightening wave with first hike in nearly 4 years "] [USN:L1N45S0Z3 TEXT:"IMF chief warns energy shock, growing debt and AI risks threaten global growth "] [USN:L6N45R0WM TEXT:"Hedge funds warn BoE repo reforms could backfire "] Today's Key Market Moves STOCKS: Japan -1%, South Korea -2%. [USN:L6N45T0EA TEXT:"Europe"] -1%, [USN:L6N45T0IE TEXT:"UK"] -0.8%. [USN:L6N45T0JD TEXT:"S&P 500 and Nasdaq"] -0.2%, Dow -0.7%. SECTORS/SHARES: Seven sectors on the S&P 500 fall, four rise. Industrials -2%, healthcare +1%. Caterpillar (CAT.N) -6%, SpaceX (SPCX.O) -2.6%. Moderna (MRNA.O) +5%, Micron Technology (MU.O) +4%. FX: US dollar back up to Monday's 17-month high, [USN:L4N45T025 TEXT:"euro"] at 17-month low. Euro/sterling down for 9th day, longest losing streak since Feb 2021. BONDS: European bonds back under pressure, French/German spread widens 10 bps to 138 bps. US 10y and 30y yields touch [USN:L8N45T0F3 TEXT:"fresh 24-year highs"] but cool after 10-year auction draws highest demand since 2016. US [USN:L6N45S1BF TEXT:"mortgage rates"] highest since 2023. COMMODITIES/METALS: [USN:L4N45T01V TEXT:"Oil"] slips - Brent -0.5%, WTI -1.3%. Gold -1%, other precious metals -3%.

Today's Talking Points: United yet divided We know that the Fed's decision to raise interest rates last month, the first hike in three years, was unanimous. What we learned from the meeting [USN:L6N45T0TQ TEXT:"minutes"] published on Wednesday is policymakers were divided on the rationale for raising rates. Some saw it as a precautionary move to cool energy-driven price pressures or inflation expectations, others saw it as the first step in a battle against demand-driven inflation. This matters because it suggests there will be less certainty and unanimity at upcoming decisions, starting with the October 28-29 meeting. The Fed rarely does "one and done" rate hikes, so it's reasonable to assume there will be more tightening to come. But how much more, and the pace, are up for more debate. This may be what Chair Kevin Warsh wants. Market pricing suggests a rate hike this month is off the table, but remember, only a week ago it was very much on the table. Three weeks is a long way away. Term premium Fed officials — and policymakers elsewhere — will surely be looking at the bond market with an increasing sense of nervousness and unease. If the rise in yields is a function of investors pricing in strong economic growth driven by demand and investment, that's one thing. If it's because of inflation fears, that's another. But if it's being driven by the 'term premium' — the extra premium investors demand for general 'risk' — then that's more worrying. And the US term premium is beginning to rise. Rapidly. It has surged 40 bps in the last two weeks, and on Monday hit a 12-year high of 96 bps. Bank of America analysts note that the term premium is also gathering force in other key bond markets, and suggest three key factors investors should watch in Q4: US fiscal and funding issues, ECB willingness to stabilize spreads, and long-end JGB dynamics. AI spaghetti The news that [USN:L6N45S1CQ TEXT:"SpaceX"] is in talks with banks and asset managers to raise $40 billion to buy Nvidia's (NVDA.O) AI chips has shone the spotlight back on the debt, deals and spaghetti-like circular financing that's driving the artificial intelligence revolution. Investors are trying to grapple with a surge in corporate bond issuance to fund AI data center construction and investment, more than $3 trillion of off-balance-sheet debt, according to Morgan Stanley, and the bilateral loans, leases and agreements between several of the big players. A growing number of investors, including veterans like Jim Chanos, Steve Eisman and Michael Burry, warn that the circularity and opacity of it all spells danger. What could move markets tomorrow? item.title: AI wants to cure disease. It needs data first
item.description: Months after the OpenClaw frenzy, personal AI agents are looking promising again.
item.dc:creator: Krystal Hu
item.content:encoded: Months after the [USN:L4N406097 TEXT:"OpenClaw frenzy"], personal AI agents are looking promising again. The latest to join the party is OpenAI, which [USN:L1N45L06P TEXT:"unveiled"] its own personal agents, “dots,” at its annual dev day last week. Meta's Muse and the startup Instinct have both launched agents that are already gaining traction, built around reading your messages and acting on your behalf. Despite a glitchy demo, OpenAI is making the case that always-on dots can chase down a user's goals across apps on their own. It’s also trying to send a message: this isn't the same breed of agent that famously[USN:L6N45H0LE TEXT:" went rogue this summer"], infiltrating everything from Hugging Face to government websites. As someone who uses these things, I keep getting stuck on the same trade-off: how much of my personal information am I willing to hand over, for how much usefulness I get back? And sometimes, the limits aren't even up to me. Businesses are increasingly blocking these agents outright, wary of losing control over their own customer relationships. Amazon, for one, has cut off Meta's Muse from shopping on its website entirely, accusing it of pulling customer data without permission. Meta says it is acting in a secure manner. It's both a security story and a turf war: every major platform wants to own its customer relationship. This week, we dive into the next frontier AI keeps promising us — curing disease. How close are we, actually, to the AI-cures-cancer headlines? Scroll on. OUR LATEST REPORTING IN TECH AND AI [USN:L8N3ZL1UG TEXT:"Companies cutting jobs as investments shift toward AI"] [USN:L4N45S0BH TEXT:"DeepSeek set to net over $12 billion in new fundraising, source says"] [USN:L4N45R19C TEXT:"Nvidia-backed Reflection unveils first AI model to take on Chinese open models"] [USN:L6N45R0XK TEXT:"McDonald's hit with class action alleging AI-powered menu price-fixing"] [USN:L4N45T0O0 TEXT:"Existential threats join bubble fears as AI mood sobers at Singapore forums"] AI'S BIOLOGY RACE By now you've probably heard, more than once, that AI is going to help us cure cancer. But how far away are we, actually? From AI labs to pharma giants to Big Tech, everyone is betting that biology is the next holy grail of AI promises. We're in the early innings, researchers and scientists told me. And one major obstacle standing between AI and drug discovery's big breakthroughs? Data. Large language models got good by scraping the internet's text — an enormous, already-existing corpus. Biology has no equivalent. There is no "internet of cells" sitting around waiting to be ingested. "We need to capture the language of biology, we need to capture the language of the cell. And that doesn't exist today," Alex Rives, head of science at the nonprofit Biohub, told me. Current cell datasets run to hundreds of millions of cells; an accurate predictive model will need billions, eventually trillions. That gap — several orders of magnitude — is the real bottleneck for now, Rives said. So Biohub is trying to build that dataset from scratch, and has [USN:L6N45T078 TEXT:"rallied an unusual coalition"] to do it: the US government, Google, and Meta have joined the project, bringing total investment to $1.8 billion. Rives says the group is compressing work that would normally take decades into five years, with a first dataset expected to be ready in about a year, and usable models possible within five. Even then, the path from dataset to actual treatment is uncertain. Rives said researchers can only begin training models once the data exists, then test whether those models can accurately predict how a cell responds to change. If that works, it could help scientists pinpoint exactly which part of a diseased cell to target. Some are already taking the experiments into the physical world. Danaher, the life sciences giant, said this week it plans to launch its [USN:L4N45T0TZ TEXT:"first AI-powered autonomous research lab"] by early 2027, aiming to design, build, and test new antibodies up to eight times faster than conventional methods. Anthropic is making a similar bet. The company has quietly set up its own [USN:L6N45814Q TEXT:"wet lab"] in the Bay Area, where human scientists and AI agents work side by side. Eric Kauderer-Abrams, Anthropic's head of life sciences, told my colleague that the final test for any biology claim still has to happen on a lab bench, not inside a model. Anthropic says it isn't chasing drug discovery for now; it's targeting neglected corners of basic biology instead. While the industry waits for a full "virtual cell," it's also trying to make some corners of the predictions work today: a wave of AI companies are running virtual drug trials, simulating how an experimental medicine might perform before it ever reaches a real patient. The stakes are real. The biopharma industry spends roughly $140 billion a year on human clinical testing, and only about 12% of drug candidates ever win regulatory approval — a rate that's barely budged in decades. One startup, BioinvestGPT, says it [USN:L1N45M12V TEXT:"correctly predicted"] the outcome of five of six high-profile trials ahead of time, including, this past July, forecasting that Novartis' muscular dystrophy drug would fall short — months before the actual trial missed its goal and erased $30 billion in market value. The simulation side of this is already saving companies money and time. The "cure cancer" side is a different story — one that might require building a model that doesn't exist yet, at a scale nobody has ever attempted. Investors are pricing in the first story while trying to predict the timeline of the second.

item.title: Açúcar bruto atinge nova máxima em 19 meses; café arábica recua
item.description: Os contratos futuros de açúcar bruto na bolsa ICE atingiram uma nova máxima em 19 meses nesta quarta-feira, antes de recuarem com o abrandamento da recente onda de compras por parte dos fundos, enquanto os preços do café e do cacau também caíram.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Os contratos futuros de açúcar bruto na bolsa ICE atingiram uma nova máxima em 19 meses nesta quarta-feira, antes de recuarem com o abrandamento da recente onda de compras por parte dos fundos, enquanto os preços do café e do cacau também caíram. AÇÚCAR * O açúcar bruto ficou praticamente inalterado no final do pregão, a 20,83 centavos por libra-peso, após ter atingido mais cedo máxima de 21,24 centavos. * Operadores afirmaram que a alta nos preços contribuiu para a fraqueza da demanda no mercado físico. * Eles observaram que a alta foi impulsionada, em parte, pelas chuvas no Brasil, que devem reduzir a produção de açúcar nesta safra. * "As chuvas no centro-sul do Brasil retardaram a colheita, o que significa que agora parece provável que a produção de açúcar fique aquém das 39 milhões de toneladas previstas pela OIA há seis semanas", afirmou a Organização Internacional do Açúcar em um relatório divulgado nesta quarta-feira * O fenômeno climático El Niño também foi visto como um fator que restringiu a produção do adoçante, particularmente na Ásia. * O preço do açúcar branco também apresentou poucas variações, ficando em US$555,70 por tonelada métrica CAFÉ * O café arábica fechou em queda de 11,75 centavos, ou 3,9%, a US$2,927 por libra-peso, revertendo em grande parte os fortes ganhos da sessão anterior; o mercado havia subido 4,1% na terça-feira. * Os corretores afirmaram que o forte ritmo das exportações do Brasil, principal produtor, garantiu que haja atualmente oferta abundante. * As exportações brasileiras de café verde em setembro totalizaram 235.800 toneladas métricas, ou 3,93 milhões de sacas de 60 kg, o maior volume em 20 meses, de acordo com dados do governo divulgados na terça-feira * No entanto, as preocupações de que o fenômeno El Niño reduza a produção global na safra 2027/28 continuaram a sustentar os preços, enquanto os estoques certificados nas bolsas também permanecem baixos * O café robusta registrou queda de 2,9%, para US$ 3.485 por tonelada CACAU * O cacau de Londres fechou em queda de £57, ou 1,3%, a £4.174 por tonelada. * Os corretores observaram que as chuvas previstas devem melhorar as perspectivas para as safras na Costa do Marfim, principal produtora. * "As chuvas que se aproximam vão amenizar significativamente as preocupações com a seca na principal safra de cacau da Costa do Marfim, mas podem não ser suficientes para garantir a recuperação dos frutos novos", afirmou a LSEG Research and Insights em uma nota * O cacau de Nova York recuou 2,1%, para US$5.582 por tonelada. (Reportagem de Nigel Hunt e Marcelo Teixeira)

item.title: Missouri sued over alleged decades of underfunding at historically Black university
item.description: Seven current and former students at Lincoln University of Missouri sued the state on Wednesday, alleging it violated the US Constitution and federal civil rights law by systematically underfunding the historically Black university for decades.
item.dc:creator: Bianca Flowers
item.content:encoded: Seven current and former students at Lincoln University of Missouri sued the state on Wednesday, alleging it violated the US Constitution and federal civil rights law by systematically underfunding the historically Black university for decades. The complaint, filed in federal court in the US District Court for the Western District of Missouri Central Division, seeks compensatory damages under Title VI of the Civil Rights Act for what plaintiffs describe as "educational and economic injuries" caused by decades of underfunding. It also seeks an injunction requiring Missouri to fully match Lincoln University's federal land-grant funding in the future. Some of the funding they are requesting would include campus repairs, faculty hiring, student services, financial aid and agricultural research programs. Lincoln University, in Jefferson City, is the state's first historically Black land-grant institution. The University of Missouri is the state's predominantly white land-grant institution.
